title: No solution (parallel, distinct lines)
subtitle: Systems of two linear equations in two variables · 20 official questions

sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **20 of the official questions in Systems of two linear equations in two variables are this one** — 0 Easy, 3 Medium, 17 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- You are asked for the constant that makes it happen, which second equation could complete such a system, or which of four systems has no solution.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Rewrite both equations in the same form.
- 2) Make the x and y coefficients proportional, so the slopes are equal, and solve for the constant.
- 3) Check that the constants are NOT in that same ratio, so the lines are different.
- When you are comparing whole systems, eliminate a variable: a false statement like 0 = 7 means no solution.

sections.heading: Where Desmos fits
body: Add a slider for the constant and look for the value where the lines become parallel and stop crossing.
For 'which system', graph each pair and look for parallel lines.
Zoom out so a far-away intersection doesn't fool you.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You pick the constant that makes the lines identical (infinitely many solutions) instead of parallel.
Or you set the slopes equal but mix up the coefficients because the equations were in different forms, for example one in y = mx + b with the other not rearranged.
